title: Your tag is not on the server (git push does not push tags)
summary: You tagged the release and pushed. CI never fired, because tags do not travel with a normal push. Learn the three ways to publish them and how to delete one that went out wrong.
mental_model: `git push` publishes branches. Tags are a separate namespace and need to be named explicitly, or swept up with `--tags` or `--follow-tags`. Nothing about tagging is automatic.

steps.title: Push the branch and check the server
steps.why: The commits arrive. The tags do not. This is the moment a release pipeline that triggers on tags silently does nothing at all.
steps.expect: Local tags listed; the remote tag listing is empty.

verify.label: a normal push published no tags

steps.title: Push one tag by name
steps.why: Naming the tag pushes exactly that tag. This is the safest form — you publish what you meant to publish and nothing else.

verify.label: the named tag reached the server

steps.title: Push every tag you have
steps.why: `--tags` sweeps up all of them, including local scratch tags you never meant to share. Convenient, and the usual reason repositories accumulate tags called `test` and `tmp`.
steps.expect: v1.1.0 and broken-release both published — the second one by accident.

steps.title: Delete the tag that should not have gone out
steps.why: Same refspec logic as branches: `--delete` removes it from the server. Your local copy is untouched, so you must delete both.

verify.label: the accidental tag is gone from the server
…and locally too — they are separate deletions

steps.title: The flag worth defaulting to
steps.why: `--follow-tags` pushes annotated tags that point at commits you are pushing anyway. It publishes release tags without sweeping up local junk — the sensible middle ground.
steps.expect: v1.2.0 published; the lightweight scratch-note is not.

steps.title: See it from a colleague's clone
steps.why: Tags arrive on fetch. A clone made before the tags existed sees them only after fetching — and `--tags` fetches tags even from commits not on any branch you track.
steps.expect: No tags at first, then all the published ones.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.why: `push.followTags true` applies the middle-ground behaviour to every push. Release tags publish themselves; scratch tags stay on your machine.

verify.label: all three release tags are on the server
no junk tags were published
verify.hint: delete the accidental one with git push origin --delete

verify.label: the colleague's clone received the tags after fetching

pitfalls: A CI pipeline triggered by tags will not run if you forget to push the tag. The commit arriving is not the trigger.
`git push --tags` publishes every local tag, including experiments. Prefer `--follow-tags` or naming the tag.
Deleting a remote tag does not delete anyone's local copy. Colleagues who already fetched keep it until they prune tags explicitly.
`git fetch` does fetch tags reachable from fetched branches, but `--tags` is needed for the rest. `git fetch --prune --prune-tags` cleans up deleted ones.
